content: ## Summary
Some customers have reported that streaming responses on Redwood’s OpenAI-compatible API may end early (without the terminal `[DONE]` event). The HTTP status is frequently 200 and the client receives partial tokens before the stream disconnects.
This is most frequently observed in **eu-west** and appears correlated with periods where upstream token generation is temporarily quiet long enough to trigger a gateway read/idle timeout."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/streaming-hangs-sse-timeouts.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Streaming chat responses can hang or stall (SSE): symptoms, causes, and workarounds", "status": "published", "date": "2025-12-12", "text": "h1. Customer-visible symptoms
* Stream starts and then stops emitting chunks (customer wording: "hang", "freeze", "stuck").
* No explicit error returned by the API; request appears in-flight indefinitely.
* Some clients retry and create duplicate assistant messages.
Common alternate descriptions seen in tickets:
* "SSE freezes"
* "stream stops after first chunk"
* "never sends [DONE]"
* "EventSource waits forever"
h1. Likely causes (multiple can apply)
h2. 1) Network/proxy idle timeouts when the stream goes quiet
If the backend pauses token emission (e.g., long decode steps, tool-calling, or internal buffering), some proxies/load balancers may consider the connection idle and interfere.
Mitigation:
* Ensure the gateway emits *SSE heartbeat frames* (comment line) when no tokens are emitted.
* For customer-managed proxies (NGINX), disable response buffering and increase read timeouts."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/overload-errors-and-retry-guidance.json", "chunk": "15/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API overload errors: support guidance, retry/backoff, and escalation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-12-05", "text": "## Escalation template (copy/paste)

body: ## Purpose
What happens when a Free workspace uses up its monthly included usage.
## Limits
- Free includes a fixed monthly amount of billed tokens and requests.
- Free has no overage: nothing beyond the included usage is ever charged, and Free workspaces never get an invoice.
## At the limit
Once a Free workspace reaches its monthly limit, further requests are rate-limited: the API returns HTTP `429` with error code `quota_exceeded` and a `Retry-After` header. Requests work again when the next month starts. To keep sending requests sooner, the customer upgrades to a paid plan.
